headline: Fed holds rates, but two officials vote for a hike
detail: The Fed kept its rate at 3.75%–4% in a 10-2 vote, with Governor Cook and Cleveland Fed President Hammack wanting a quarter-point hike; traders now put about 85% odds on a December hike and the 10-year yield went back above 5%. Higher rates and a firmer dollar are a headwind for metal prices.

headline: Copper holds near a two-week high as China's import premium hits a decade-plus high
detail: LME copper eased about 0.3% to roughly $14,430 a ton early Thursday after a two-week high Wednesday, while the Yangshan import premium rose to $205 a ton and Shanghai exchange stocks fell more than 26% last week. Tight Chinese supply keeps a floor under copper and copper scrap bids.

headline: Chicago yard expects ferrous scrap to rise again in November
detail: BL Duke expects another increase across all grades in November after October's $30 per gross ton rise, citing full mill order books, busheling futures above $500 and lean yard inventories. That points to firmer prices for shred, HMS and busheling.

headline: Ford raises its commodity cost estimate to about $2.5 billion
detail: Ford lifted its full-year commodity cost estimate from about $2 billion, pointing to higher copper and steel prices, while Q3 core profit edged up to $2.7 billion and it raised the low end of its profit guidance. It said recovery from the Novelis aluminum plant fire is largely behind it.

headline: Gold flat, silver down 1% after the Fed
detail: Gold ended Wednesday near $4,057, down just $2.50, while silver fell about 1.1% to $53.72 as hike odds rose, Brent stayed above $115 and the 10-year yield hovered near 5%. Both slid further overnight, with gold near $4,025.

headline: Iron ore sinks to its lowest since September 2024
detail: Singapore iron ore futures touched $89.25 a ton Tuesday as Chinese mills buy only what they need heading into the slow winter season and big miners ship more. One analyst sees $85–86 in November, which keeps pressure on steel and ferrous scrap.

headline: China plans at least 2.2 trillion yuan of bond sales in November–December
detail: Central and local governments plan to raise at least 2.2 trillion yuan (about $330 billion) in the last two months of the year, the second-largest amount on record for that period. More infrastructure money would help Chinese steel and copper demand.

headline: Workers block Codelco's Ministro Hales copper mine in Chile
detail: Workers blocked access to the Chilean mine for about six hours Monday over unpaid bonuses, the latest in a run of supply problems. Disruptions in Chile add to copper's tight supply picture.

headline: Teck's Highland Valley mine runs at reduced capacity during strike
detail: More than 1,200 Steelworkers walked out Oct. 24 at Canada's biggest copper mine over pay, pensions and staffing, and Teck says output is reduced. A long strike tightens North American copper supply.

headline: Nucor lifts spot hot-rolled coil to $1,270 a ton
detail: Nucor raised its weekly spot HRC price $15 to $1,270 per short ton, its 14th straight weekly increase, with lead times of three to five weeks. Strong mill pricing supports demand for prime and shredded scrap.

headline: Canada says only limited progress in US tariff talks
detail: A Canadian official said talks on easing US Section 232 tariffs, up to 50% on steel and 25% on autos, have made limited progress, even as both sides work toward a deal. A deal could bring more Canadian steel and aluminum south and soften US premiums.

headline: Nucor: scrap costs flat, fourth quarter steady
detail: Nucor earned $5.80 a share in Q3 and paid an average $421 per gross ton for scrap and substitutes, about the same as Q2. It sees Q4 earnings flat to slightly higher, a sign the biggest US scrap buyer expects steady mill demand.

headline: LME aluminum edges up as stocks stay thin
detail: Three-month LME aluminum rose 0.3% to about $3,098 a ton Wednesday on supply worries, with LME stocks near 232,000 tons; zinc gained while nickel, lead and tin slipped. Firm aluminum supports cast, extrusion and can prices.

headline: Platinum dips below $1,500 as PGMs fall about 4% on the week
detail: Platinum briefly fell under $1,500 an ounce and palladium sat near $1,010 as December hike odds and investor selling weighed. Lower PGM prices mean lower catalytic converter payouts.

headline: Freeport's Q3 copper output drops 8.8%; Grasberg at two-thirds capacity
detail: Freeport produced about 377,000 tons of copper in Q3, down 8.8% from a year ago, and its outlook implies 2026 output about 8% below 2025 with Grasberg near 67% of capacity. Less mine supply keeps copper and scrap demand strong.

headline: Builder confidence falls to its lowest since 2012
detail: The NAHB builder index fell 3 points to 29 in October and a record 43% of builders cut prices, while pending home sales hit a record low with 30-year mortgages above 7%. Weak housing means less demand for copper wire, plumbing and building steel.

headline: Cox sees October new-vehicle sales up 7% from a year ago
detail: Cox Automotive forecasts about 1.38 million October sales and a 16.1 million annual pace, up from 15.7 million last year. Steady sales keep auto plants running and scrap flowing.

headline: Gold funds lose money while Asian buyers step in
detail: Gold ETFs had $1.1 billion of net outflows in the week to Oct. 23, including $1.7 billion from North America, while Indian bullion premiums rose to $15 an ounce. Physical buying is helping hold gold near $4,000.

headline: Indonesia warns 2027 nickel quota requests are too big
detail: Indonesia's mining chief said 2027 nickel ore requests top 500 million tons and approving too much could flood the market; ore prices were flat Thursday. More Indonesian ore keeps nickel and stainless scrap prices soft.

headline: Stellantis: North American shipments down 12% in Q3
detail: Stellantis said North American shipments fell to 357,000 after a planned Grand Cherokee and Compass shutdown, and it expects about €1 billion in tariff costs this year. It kept its full-year outlook and expects more shipments in Q4, which means more auto scrap and steel demand.

headline: Analysts cut platinum and palladium forecasts again
detail: A Reuters survey shows analysts lowered their 2026 platinum and palladium price outlooks for a third straight quarter, citing high rates and a strong dollar. That points to softer catalytic converter values.

headline: Converter average slips to about $88 a unit
detail: RRCats' national average was $87.83 a converter on Oct. 28, down from about $90 two days earlier, with PGM prices lower. Expect bids to stay soft while platinum and palladium sit near yearly lows.

headline: China's copper scrap imports jump 33% in September
detail: China imported about 237,000 tons of copper scrap in September, up 33% from August, as its import window opened; US shipments are recovering from a very low base. Strong Chinese demand helps support copper scrap prices.

headline: China factory profits rise 14.4% in September
detail: Chinese industrial profits grew at the fastest pace since June, led by AI-related and mining sectors, while consumer industries lagged. Better profits help metals demand but lower the odds of new stimulus.

headline: China's big mills cut daily steel output 2.3% in mid-October
detail: CISA member mills averaged 1.89 million tons a day Oct. 11–20 while finished steel stocks rose 1.5%. Lower Chinese output weighs on iron ore and global steel prices.

headline: New home sales slip to a 676,000 pace in September
detail: Sales of new homes dipped 0.6% from August and are down 5% from a year ago, though they beat forecasts; supply sits at 8.4 months. Slow housing means less demand for copper wire, plumbing and building steel.

headline: Copper miners rally; odds of a copper cable tariff near 25%
detail: Southern Copper jumped 4.5% and Freeport 1.2% Tuesday. Prediction markets give about a 25% chance of US tariffs on insulated copper cable by year-end, which would affect wire scrap flows.

headline: Consumer confidence jumps to its best since June
detail: The Conference Board index rose 7.5 points to 91.7 in October as gas prices eased, the first gain in four months. Stronger consumers help car and appliance demand but can also push the Fed toward a hike.

headline: Trump orders talks, not tariffs yet, on machinery imports
detail: A new Section 232 action on robotics and industrial machinery tells Commerce and the trade office to negotiate with trading partners rather than set tariff rates now. It shows the administration keeps widening its Section 232 tools beyond steel and aluminum.
